Review Title: Wonderful customer service despite the disappointing weather
Review Text:
Our family booked the 30 minute seaplane adventure as part of our cruisetour. Due to rainy weather, we were not able to take the tour but I wanted to acknowledge the wonderful customer service provided. The company reached out the day before to let us know the weather did not look good for our flight but they would keep us informed. We had booked a morning flight. They contacted us in the morning to confirm we would have to cancel but offered to postpone to another day. Unfortunately we were leaving the next day to go to Denali so they offered to wait until afternoon and see if the weather cleared. We were contacted again at noon time and weather was still not cooperating so they had to cancel. Our payment was refunded in full with no headaches. Although we obviously would have preferred to be able to take the seaplane flight, weather is the determining factor on adventures like these. I was so grateful for the wonderful customer service. I felt the company cared and really tried to find a way for us to enjoy our excursion.
For anyone planning an Alaskan adventure, feel comfortable booking with this company knowing they try there best to fulfill their commitment and when they are not able to, you will be refunded quickly and without any hassles.

Review Title: Awesome Hike but NOT at Denali National Park
Review Text: This is a bit of a mixed experience for us.  The floatplane ride to Caribou lodge was wonderful - the guided hike from Caribou Lodge at Boomerang Lake was really awesome - Zack showed us amazing tundra plant life - his family at Caribou lodge opened our eyes with their lifestyle and their hospitality.  So full points to them for our delightful hiking experience.  But due to cloudy conditions  the flight service to view Denali National Park from the air was canceled (the float plane service reimbursed us very promptly for the missed portion of the trip).  Here's my issue - the blurb states "Experience Denali National Park from the air and at ground level"  The clouds made us miss the "from the air portion" and we accept with gratitude what Mother Nature grants us, but there was *never* a chance of experiencing Denali NP "at ground level."  So by following this ad, we missed out on visiting Denali National Park on a once in a lifetime trip to Alaska, and that was disappointing indeed.  The ad needs to be clear that there is NEVER a chance to experience Denali National Park *at ground level* with this service. If the weather permits, you see DNP from the air, but you never get to DNP at ground level, no matter what.

Review Text: We saw that the weather was going to be clear for the several days that we were in Talkeetna (late August '16) and booked a flight-seeing tour with this company.  The weather was probably as good as could be hoped for-- blue skies, few clouds, little to no wind, temperatures in the upper 60's.  We departed at noon, with the sun overhead. My wife and I thoroughly enjoyed the experience.  The flight path took us thru some of the most spectacular vistas that we've ever seen.  We opted for the lake landing, and were not disappointed.  The aircraft had a smooth landing, and when it came to a stop the aircraft was pointed directly at Mt. Denali.  The pilot asked us if we wanted to get out of the aircraft and stand on the landing pontoons (which I did).  Took some video and photos from this location.  The pilot took a photo of me standing on the pontoon and holding onto the wing strut, with Denali in the background.  My wife and I both agree that this was the highlight of our Alaska trip.  The cost was a bit pricey, but we thought it was worth it (most likely a once in a lifetime experience).

Review Text:

When I asked to use the bathroom they explained their bathroom was out of service and I could use the woods behind the fuel truck filling up - um, okay. Next they strongly suggested I leave a tip on the $840 price tag - we opted to see how the flight went first.
I understand a father and son own the plane company and we were sent out with the son as our pilot. While he was clean cut and appeared to be a good pilot he lacked personality. The entire flight was mostly spent in silence, he didn't provide any info about the area, history and briefly described what we saw. When I inquired about the history of Talkeenta he suggested I visit the history museum in town.
Our friends flew on K2 Avaition next door and said they had a wonderful time and their pilot was super friendly and provided a ton of information. My suggestion would be to see if you can book with them first. We definitely wouldn't recommend this company if you're looking for more than just a plane ride. Review Text: Unfortunately, this was the one cloudy and overcast day on our trip to Denali.  Would have been so much better on a clear day! It is very easy to find - just turn right onto the road to Talkeetna, and it will soon be on your right side.  We selected Alaska Bush Float Plane over K2 or Talkeetna Air Taxi because we wanted to go in a float plane - taking off and landing on the water was a new experience for us!  We did the basic tour and thought that was just the right amount of time.  We did get to see the top of Denali when we got above the clouds, and were able to see glaciers.  Like others have said - the pilot (Jason, I think?) is not overly chatty.  We found him to be nice and pleasant - not rude at all - just a quite guy. Review Title: Scared to Death but WORTH IT!
Review Text: I am a terrible flier. As in PETRIFIED.  Somehow, though, this clean, well kept little dock caught my eye as my husband and I drove into Talkeetna for one overnight. Despite my fear, I thought about it all night and when we pulled out the following afternoon, there it was, calling to me.  I would like to say that I got over my fear but I didn't... I pushed through and boarded the tiniest little float plane with my husband, another frightened lady, and the pilot who was in his early 20's and had been flying solo since he was 16.  I remained petrified and with my eyes closed for the first 10 minutes, he did offer to turn back (maybe he heard me hyperventilating?) but I stuck it out.  Wildlife didn't cooperate, no bears or eagles to be seen, but the 30 minute flight was handled safely and professionally, with beautiful scenery and a blue sky day.  I had faith in the pilot, who really was awesome, and he landed us down on the lake smooth as glass. I think I can cross this off my bucket list and am glad I had this experience with such a great organization...

Review Text:
My cousin told us that the very best use of our money in Alaska would be on a scenic flight around Mt. McKinley. Even though they are expensive, she told us they are worth every penny. So, I went inside to check out K2 Aviation. There were so many options: the McKinley Experience, the McKinley Flyer, or as long as you're spending that much money, do you go all out for the Denali Grand Tour? And then should we add a glacier landing? There wasn't much of a discount for kids; they actually recommend having parents take turns and go one at a time while the other parent stays with the kids and plays on the playground. I didn't like that idea at all, and it was raining. And then I realized we had missed the first flight on the schedule and would have to wait for the next one, a few hours later in the afternoon. And if it was raining in Talkeetna, would we even be able to see Mt. McKinley? We drove away and started to leave Talkeetna. But then my husband spotted the float planes and decided we needed to stop and check them out.

He has a thing for float planes (from watching Northern Exposure); he's also attracted to buildings with vegetation growing on the roof. The sign says Mt. McKinley Scenic, but the business is called The Alaska Bush Float Plane Service.

My husband was sold with the idea of landing on a lake. And Molly, the woman who sets up the flights couldn't have been more accommodating. The planes only hold five passengers, but Molly quickly offered to babysit our youngest while the rest of us went on a flight. Perfect! (She told us kids under the age of five usually fell asleep anyway.) She went and talked to the pilot and came back with a reasonable discounted family price. I couldn't decide whether to take the Explore Denali 1.0 Tour or the Explore Denali 1.2 Tour. (The 1.2 Tour is about fifteen minutes longer, takes you over the Climber's Base Camp area, and offers a view of the West Buttress Route that is used by most climbers.) So Molly told me we could decide in the air. Perfect again!

We flew over the Talkeetna airport, over some rivers, up and over the clouds, and then we were in the mountains. I could not believe the view! The glacier lakes were incredible. It looked like someone had dropped blue food coloring onto the snow. We flew right by the south face of Mt. McKinley. But without our pilot, we really wouldn't have been able to identify which one it was. All of the mountains were magnificent. And we were so close!

It was probably ten minutes into our flight before I realized I had a two-way radio on my headset. Our three kids didn't know they had radios until the end of the flight; we didn't tell them because I didn't want them all trying to talk to the pilot at once. I had them raise their hands when they wanted to talk, and then I passed them my microphone.

We should have prepped the kids with some information before the trip because they were full of curiosity. I tried to limit their questions to the pilot because I didn't want them to distract him. Jason, how deep is that snow? Jason, which one is Moose's Tooth? Jason, which one is a glacier?

Without an aerial tour, it is impossible to comprehended the staggering depth of the Alaska Range. There were so many things to see that it was hard to decide which direction to look. The view was surprisingly clear. (Mt. McKinley is so large that it creates its own localized weather.) We decided to fly over the Climber's Base Camp. We were also able to (barely) spot some climbers on the mountain.

The questions continued. Jason, how many people climb Mt. McKinley? (About 1200 per year; roughly half succeed.) Jason, how long does it take to climb Mt. McKinley? (About two or three weeks.) Jason, has anyone ever died trying to climb Mt. McKinley? (120. . . and counting. Four Japanese climbers died in an avalanche just one week after our visit.)

By the way, I just looked these answers up myself. I couldn't remember his responses because I was too busy trying to keep my girls quiet. Our pilot was nice, but he didn't seem accustomed to endless questions from eight and nine-year-olds.

That is one thing they could have improved on. Also, they had my kids sit on life jackets to boost them up to be able to see out of the plane windows. Real booster seats would have been more comfortable.

The views were breathtaking. It was another pinch-yourself-I-can't-believe-we-are-really-doing-this-moment. And then our landing on Fish Lake was fantastic.

What an amazing experience! And how glad I am that we stopped to check out The Alaska Bush Float Plane Service. They are a small, family-owned business and were able to personalize the trip just for us. I'm pretty sure that was the most expensive "impulse purchase" I've ever made, but it was well worth the price.

Review Text: My family and I decided to take the longer Denali Flightseeing tour after many phone calls with Alaska Bush Floatplane's office staff. I spoke to both Molly and Nancy on different occasions and they were very pleasant and helpful in gearing me towards the flight tour that we would all enjoy. They have six tours to choose from and they also offer hiking and fishing trips that vary in time and price. We arrived early in the morning with coffee in hand from the nearby bakery and we sat on their deck while watching the swans swim in the lake. I had seen photos on their Facebook page of others enjoying the deck and the swans, so we made sure to arrive early to do the same. It is by far the most beautiful place in Talkeetna. They have dahlias blooming in every corner, and the log cabin is a nice authentic touch!  The pilot offered a detailed safety briefing before we loaded the plane, and we were promptly on our way to see Denali on a very beautiful day. I was worried about my first flight in a small plane but it was very smooth, especially in comparison to my flight into Anchorage on a large commercial jet. We all loved being able to see out of every window and in every direction. Flying over glaciers and around the mountains of Denali National Park was amazing. The pilot was very informative and we all learned a thing or two about living in Alaska's bush. My entire experience with this company was excellent and it was the best tour we took while in Alaska.  I do recommend using this tour company while in Alaska.
